title: Genres as Teachers

learn.summary: Each genre is a masterclass in one skill: street teaches timing, portraiture teaches people and light, landscape teaches patience and planning, macro teaches pure seeing. Rotating through them builds a complete photographer faster than staying comfortable in one. Your phone handles all four.

do: Pick the genre that intimidates you most and give it one dedicated 30-minute session this week.

children.title: Street

learn.summary: Street photography teaches anticipation — Henri Cartier-Bresson's "decisive moment" is the instant when geometry and life align, and it rewards those already in position. Work a promising background and wait for the right passerby to enter it. A phone is the ideal street camera: silent, unthreatening, always present.

do: Find one strong background in your town this week, stand still for ten minutes, and photograph the moments people bring to it.

children.title: Portrait

learn.summary: Portraits teach light and rapport in equal measure: window light at 45 degrees, subject's near eye sharp, background quiet. The technical half is learnable in a week; the human half — making someone comfortable enough to look like themselves — is the lifetime skill. Talk more than you shoot.

do: Make a window-light portrait of a friend or family member this week: seat them at 45 degrees to the window, focus on the near eye, take 20 frames, gift them the best.

children.title: Landscape

learn.summary: Landscape teaches planning and patience: the photo is decided by when you arrive (golden hour, weather fronts) and where you stand, long before the shutter opens. Classic craft: foreground interest anchors the frame, f/8–f/11 keeps it deep, and the horizon obeys the thirds. The genre's dirty secret is that it is mostly walking and waiting.

do: Scout one local viewpoint in daylight, then return at golden hour this week with a foreground object already chosen — shoot ten deliberate frames.

children.title: Macro & Detail

learn.summary: Macro shrinks the world to textures, droplets, and insect geographies, and it retrains the eye to find photographs within arm's reach — a kitchen table becomes a landscape. Depth of field at close range is millimeters, so focus becomes surgical. Phone macro modes and cheap clip-on lenses put the genre within anyone's budget.

do: Spend 20 minutes photographing only things smaller than your thumb — at home or in a garden — and keep your five best textures.
